items.title: $799 Smart Glasses Promise Vision Pro-Style Controls in a 45g Frame
items.excerpt: Hong Kong startup Savage Technology has announced its first product, "Orrorin Glasses," promising Vision Pro-style pinch controls and full-color displays for both eyes in a frame weighing just 45 grams. The company describes the glasses as offering "Vision Pro–level interaction" and being around 25 times lighter than Apple's headset, including its external battery.
items.rationale: A new product announcement with a price: $799 glasses with binocular color displays and pinch input at 45 g. It is a new smart-glasses interaction claim from a company that does not appear in the 30-day history.

items.title: Wyze's new window feeder records birds from a camera inside your home
items.excerpt: Wyze launched the $70 Window Bird Cam, a window-mounted feeder whose camera sits inside the home and uses AI to identify bird species.
items.rationale: A product launch at a consumer price ($70), with on-device AI species identification. It is one story across two outlets (cluster c7), so the Verge copy is kept and the 9to5Google copy is dropped.

items.title: Child safety groups across the world are begging Amazon to remove AI toys for kids
items.excerpt: A plush bunny marketed for ages 3 and up reportedly connects to chatbots whose own terms say 13 and older.
items.rationale: A distinct new action: an international coalition of child-safety groups petitioning Amazon to delist AI toys, with a mismatch between the product's age rating and the chatbot's terms. The curator brief marks it as separate from the New York ban, which politics has already published.

items.title: Rogbid's Loop Memo Puts a Voice Recorder and Health Tracker on Your Wrist
items.excerpt: A voice recorder that lives on your wrist and never asks for a subscription fee is a pitch I can get behind. Rogbid's Loop Memo records with one press, then
items.rationale: A new wearable: a one-press AI voice recorder combined with a health band, with no subscription. It is a new form factor in the AI note-taker category, unlike the Anker, Flowtica and Comulytic devices published earlier.

items.title: Google Home gets another big update with these new app, Nest Cam, and Gemini features
items.excerpt: Google Home is rolling out another big update, this time adding features and bringing improvements across Nest Cam, Nest Thermostarts,...
items.rationale: A new rollout (the 11-25 Google Home release) with fresh Nest Cam and Gemini features. It is a separate release from the 11-11 update and the 11-17 announcement, so it is labelled as a follow-up.

https://9to5google.com/2026/11/25/google.new_action: New 11-25 Google Home release rolling out Nest Cam, Nest Thermostat, app and Gemini changes (distinct from the 11-11 update and the 11-17 feature announcement https://9to5google.com/2026/11/17/google-home-new-features-nest-thermostat-upgrades/)

dedup.note: Pool of 14. CROSS-SECTION DROP: the whole New York AI-chatbot-toy ban cluster — TechCrunch, The Verge, TechRadar, Notebookcheck, and Gizmodo 'AI Toys Are a Nightmare Before Christmas' (built on the same signing). Politics already published the primary source on 11-25 (governor.ny.gov 'Governor Hochul Signs Five-Year Ban on AI Chatbot Toys'), and a story may run in only one section. Within-pool drop: the 9to5Google Wyze Window Bird Cam (same story as the Verge copy, cluster c7). Content drop: CNET 'Apple Watch audio intelligence' hands-on. It is a review of the watchOS 27.3 Live Rewind/Siri Recap features published 11-04 (macrumors), with no new release. Quality drops: Tapo C825 (the AI is incidental; it is a touchscreen/video-call camera), and the Gizmodo 'AI Earbuds Are Being Held Back by Their AI' column (commentary, already dropped on 11-25, echoes the 11-09 Tom's Guide piece). Timing: every pick except Wyze was published after the 11-25 07:00 KST run, so none can be in published_urls.json. Wyze (11-24 15:14 UTC) predates that run but is absent from the gadgets 30-day digest and the politics digest, and the brief lists no cross-section assignment for it. Diversity: 5 distinct outlets, 1 each.
